answer: Admission ties a seat to one aid-to-navigation on the coast guard light list: a number, coordinates, the flash period. The node reads that list, then wants three vessels to log the signal on the correct bearing during the quarter, each entry signed by the watch officer. A copied number points at an unlit tower, so a voyage past it files nothing. Fifty clones need fifty lit stations: tower 40,000 dollars, lantern and optic 18,000, solar 9,000, upkeep 3,500 a year, near 3.5 million before one hull sights a flash. A quill fills a logbook from memory; a bearing has to be taken from the deck.
